subject: Temporary escalation lattice & P1/P2 SLA carveout for APAC edge maintenance
messages:
From: Sara Mendez <sara.m@fintegrate.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintegrate.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA adjustment for APAC maintenance window

Hi Karthik,

Heads up — we have a scheduled infrastructure maintenance at our APAC edge provider the week of July 15 that will require a controlled cutover of connectors and may affect traffic routing into Redwood for up to 8 hours overnight SGT. Our ops team described a plausible increase in incident noise during that window and asked whether we can get a temporary carveout to the standard P1/P2 response windows and on-call routing so we can avoid double-incidents while we rehome endpoints.

Key asks from our side:
- Temporary P1 response target relaxed from 15 min -> 30 min for the window (only during 00:00–08:00 SGT on July 16–17).
- P2 response target relaxed from 60 min -> 120 min for the same window.
- Confirmed on-call handover plan and escalation contacts for APAC overnight so our teams have a single routing target.

Attached is our maintenance plan and timeline. We can sign an addendum; procurement asked for the SLO language and a proposed escalation matrix.

Appreciate a quick read — we need to finalize procurement language by next Friday (July 1).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Mendez
Head of Platform Ops, Fintegrate
[sent from mobile]

[Attachment: fintegrate-maintenance-plan.pdf (PDF, 238KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.m@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA adjustment for APAC maintenance window

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. I reviewed the maintenance plan briefly; the timeline and scope are clear. We can support a timeboxed operational carveout but need to lock down routing and escalation owners before we commit.

Immediate asks from our side to make procurement comfortable:
1) Exact windows in UTC (you mentioned SGT — please confirm start/end times).
2) A single technical point of contact from Fintegrate for real-time coordination.
3) Confirmation on whether BGP/draining will be staged (affects how quickly we can failover).

Proposed operational approach (high level):
- Accept a temporary P1 -> 30 min / P2 -> 120 min only for the named windows.
- Implement an "escalation lattice": primary APAC on-call -> secondary EU ops -> regional SRE across Redwood Dedicated; each step has a 15 min handover SLA. This gives you continuity if the local APAC routing path is disrupted.
- Formalize the amendment as a 48-hour addendum (effective only for July 16 00:00–07:59 SGT) and attach to the existing agreement.

I looped Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (on-call ops lead) to confirm capacity and Monica (on-call coordinator) for the rotation change.

I'll draft a short SLO amendment and escalation lattice diagram and share back by EOD. If procurement needs a signature, we can route the DocuSign once wording is final.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: slo-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA adjustment for APAC maintenance window

Thanks for looping us in. Quick notes from CS/ops perspective:
- We can sign a timeboxed carveout as long as it's explicit about the exact UTC window and the services impacted (generation vs embeddings vs management API). Need to avoid broad language like "all traffic".
- For routing: recommend we use an APAC-specific route policy in Redwood Console that pins Fintegrate traffic to the EU fallback during the window (automatic fallback will be reversible). That reduces confusion for your onsite team.
- On-call: Ben, can we commit a shadow APAC on-call for the night of July 16? If yes, we can publish the escalation lattice and share with Fintegrate. Monica please confirm the handover times you can support.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head, Customer Success — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: escalation-lattice-diagram.png (PNG, 120KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA adjustment for APAC maintenance window

We can staff a dedicated shadow on-call for that night (Jul 16). Operational notes:
- Proposed lattice: APAC shadow (primary) -> EU on-call (secondary, +1hr handover) -> Redwood SRE pager (global tertiary). Each level has an explicit runbook step: confirm degraded routing -> apply route pin -> escalate to SRE if >30 min unresolved.
- Credits: Our standard practice is to offer standby credits for maintenance-induced carveouts; procurement will want a clause. I suggest 0.5 days of service credit for each 4-hour affected window.
- We need Fintegrate to accept a narrow scope: only generation and streaming endpoints affected; embeddings & batch ingestion excluded. That reduces blast radius.

Ben
Ben Carter
Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendez <sara.m@fintegrate.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA adjustment for APAC maintenance window

Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review we've agreed the following (final proposal):

1) Effective window:
   - July 16, 2028 00:00–07:59 SGT (UTC+8) only. Translation: 2028-07-15T16:00:00Z to 2028-07-16T23:59:00Z (document will show both TZs).
2) SLO adjustments (timeboxed):
   - P1 response target for impacted services: 30 minutes (was 15).
   - P2 response target for impacted services: 120 minutes (was 60).
3) Scope: generation + streaming endpoints (explicitly excludes embeddings, batch ingestion, and data plane management APIs).
4) Escalation lattice (operational):
   - Primary: Fintegrate on-call -> Redwood APAC shadow (Ben's team) -> Redwood EU on-call -> Redwood SRE global pager. Each handover step has 15-minute acknowledgement expectation in the lattice diagram.
5) Credits & procurement: Redwood will offer a proportional standby credit (0.5 day of service credit per 4-hour affected window) if an incident is attributable to maintenance routing changes. Procurement: we attached a short amendment with the legal phrasing and a DocuSign link for signature.

Next steps:
- Sara: confirm the single technical POC and sign the DocuSign by Tues, July 2 so both procurement teams can finalize. DocuSign link: https://docusign.example.com/FT-2028-1145
- Marissa & Ben: I'll publish the temporary route policy and the escalation lattice in Console and share a 1-page runbook with Fintegrate before July 14.

If procurement needs any alternate language, flag small edits only — we want to keep this limited and reversible.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: slo-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
